tasks.title: Record repository identity at publish time

details.goal: A publish records project name, root, branch and remote in meta, and GraphMeta exposes branch and remote so status can report them.
details.contract:
meta keys written at publish time: project_name, project_root, project_branch, project_remote. meta is key/value, so there is no schema change, no migration, no drizzle edit.

GraphMeta gains two fields:
  readonly projectBranch: string | null;
  readonly projectRemote: string | null;
The existing projectName/projectRoot stay as their current types. An absent or empty stored value maps to null; an empty string must never reach the reader.

Capture:
- root  = canonical repo root (AppConfig.repoRoot, already available to the worker)
- name  = basename of that root
- branch = `git symbolic-ref --short HEAD` result, empty on a detached HEAD
- remote = `git config --get remote.origin.url` result, empty when no origin
Both git calls are best-effort in the publish path: a non-zero exit or a spawn failure records the empty string and never fails the publish, and never throws.

DATABASE.md line 180 already specifies the first two keys; this task makes the implementation match the document.
Do not change the warning in src/index.ts (the status task owns it), and do not touch src/shared/domain/freshness.ts.
Prepared statements only: any new read goes through prepared() from #shared/store/db.
steps: Add the branch and remote capture to the worker's publish path next to the existing revision capture, best-effort and non-throwing.
Write the four meta keys in persist at publish time, in the same transaction that sets meta.generation.
Extend GraphMeta and metaFor() in reader.ts, mapping absent values to null.
Extend tests/persist.test.ts: a publish writes all four keys; a missing remote records an empty value that metaFor() reports as null; a failed git call does not fail the publish.

tasks.title: Runtime preflight for a non-Bun or too-old runtime

details.goal: An invocation under a non-Bun runtime, or a Bun older than 1.4.4, prints exactly one JSON diagnostic on stderr naming the requirement and the resolved runtime, then exits non-zero with stdout untouched.
details.contract:
Exact shape to honour:

export const MIN_BUN = "1.4.4";
export function runtimeDiagnostic(runtime: { readonly bun: string | undefined; readonly node: string | undefined }): string | null;
- returns null when runtime.bun is defined and >= MIN_BUN (numeric segment compare, no dependency)
- returns a one-line JSON string otherwise, shaped like {"level":"error","msg":"runtime.unsupported","required":"Bun >= 1.4.4","found":"<bun version or node version>","resolved":"<Bin path or 'not bun'>","hint":"install Bun >= 1.4.4 and re-run"}

Wiring in bin/sangkar.ts:
- runs before the dynamic import of ../src/index, so nothing opens a database first
- writes the line to process.stderr only; stdout must stay byte-empty
- exits 70 (EX_SOFTWARE) after writing

A missing `bun` binary itself cannot be caught here: the shebang fails before any line of this file runs. Say so in a comment above the guard instead of implying coverage.
Do not add process.version parsing beyond a numeric compare, and do not add a dependency.
steps: Create src/shared/runtime.ts with MIN_BUN, the compare and runtimeDiagnostic.
Create tests/runtime.test.ts with a table: 1.4.4 ok, 1.5.0 ok, 1.4.3 refused, 1.3.9 refused, undefined bun refused, and assert the refused payload parses as JSON and names Bun >= 1.4.4.
Wire the guard into bin/sangkar.ts before the dynamic import, writing to stderr and exiting 70.
Assert in the test that the guard writes nothing to stdout, and that a supported runtime produces a null diagnostic.
Run the task verification plus a manual probe: ~/.bun/bin/bun run bin/sangkar.ts status --json still answers.
details.verify:
~/.bun/bin/bun run typecheck  (exit 0)
~/.bun/bin/bun run test tests/runtime.test.ts  (all pass)
~/.bun/bin/bun run bin/sangkar.ts status --json  (answers normally: stdout is the JSON envelope, no diagnostic line)
Done when: the refused cases produce one stderr line naming Bun >= 1.4.4 and the supported runtime is unchanged.

progress.detail: New src/shared/runtime.ts (MIN_BUN 1.4.4, numeric-segment compare, runtimeDiagnostic, guardRuntime -> RUNTIME_EXIT 70, stderr-only sink), new tests/runtime.test.ts (14 tests / 42 expects), bin/sangkar.ts guard placed before `await import("../src/index")`. Verify: `bun run typecheck` exit 0; `PATH=~/.bun/bin:$PATH bun run test tests/runtime.test.ts` 14 pass / 0 fail (the script calls `bun` from PATH, hence the prefix); `bun run bin/sangkar.ts status --json` exit 0, stdout 1185 bytes = 10-member JSON envelope status=ok, 0 runtime.unsupported lines (single stderr line is the pre-existing store.identity_unrecorded warn); real-process refusal probe exit 70, stdout 0 bytes, one stderr line {"required":"Bun >= 1.4.4","found":"1.3.9"}; biome check clean on the 3 files. Gap: under node the static `../src/shared/runtime` import fails first (ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND, exit 1, stdout 0), so the diagnostic is unreachable outside Bun; the fix is tsconfig `allowImportingTsExtensions` + a `.ts` specifier (out of scope).

Orchestrator verification: `~/.bun/bin/bun run typecheck` exit 0; `bun run test tests/runtime.test.ts` 14 pass / 0 fail / 42 expects; `bun run bin/sangkar.ts status --json` exit 0 with a normal envelope on stdout and no runtime.unsupported line on stderr. Real-process refusal probe: exit 70, stdout 0 bytes, stderr one JSON line naming Bun >= 1.4.4. Documented limit: a non-Bun interpreter cannot reach the guard because the extensionless static import of ../src/shared/runtime fails node's resolver first (ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND); the guard is Bun-reachable only, which is the stale-Bun case it exists for. No BUN_VERSION env override exists, so the phase-2 runtime probe must fake the RuntimeProbe rather than force an env var.

details.contract:
Write-side import taxonomy (issue #12). Today src/indexer/resolve.ts:358 records every failed import as "dynamic", and moduleFile returns null for both "no candidate" and "many candidates".

New API on SymbolIndex:
  moduleCandidates(module: string): readonly string[]
  - sorted repo-relative paths
  - [] when nothing matched, exactly one path when resolved, two or more when a stem tie exists
  - moduleFile must be re-expressed over it (length === 1 ? that path : null) so the two can never disagree

BindEvidenceKind becomes ["receiver_type_unknown", "ambiguous", "dynamic", "missing_module"].

In the "imports" case of bind():
- one candidate -> emit the edge exactly as today
- more than one -> unresolvedOf(context, raw, "ambiguous") with evidence `${raw.evidence} candidates: ${candidates.join(" | ")}`
- zero candidates, specifier starts with "./" or "../" -> "missing_module", evidence `${raw.evidence} (no file matched)`
- zero candidates otherwise -> "dynamic" with evidence unchanged (bare package, node:, bun:)
- specifier starting with "#" stays "dynamic": a tsconfig path alias is not resolvable by this resolver and must not be reported as a defect in the tree

No schema change: unresolved.evidence_kind is unconstrained text and persist writes whatever kind it is handed. Do not change the same-file, unique-name or inherited-call tiers, and do not touch src/indexer/persist.ts.
The evidence suffix follows a space on purpose: #shared/domain/unresolved.ts reads the specifier only up to the first space.
